# Current delivery: existing M3 generic owners and optional primitive module

The final receiving recipe is `com.synexia.m3.M3JdkCollectionCurrentOwners20261017`, bound to M3jdk21@a918e588dd11d5ff7e0a6d4efaa89bb1679a9798. During qualification the base absorbed the same original filtered wrapper owners under `com.m3.collections`. Exact package-mapped source comparison established identity. The final recipe therefore refines two private atoms in the existing M3FilteredViews and retains the existing M3MutableFilteredViews unchanged. It does not deliver the earlier duplicate generic `jdk.m3.collections` facades.

The optional `jdk.m3.collections` module now exports only `com.m3.util` primitive projections. The existing Maven `m3/collections` project remains the generic module owner; the optional profile composes it with the primitive project. Main name-mapping preserves every concurrent entry and adds only the explicit optional registration. Synexia's existing provenance ledger also retains every concurrent row before this additive delivery.

## Current-base executed proof and remaining gate

All 10 current-owner Java crates and the 10-asset text crate passed the unchanged canonical OpenRewrite SDK with exact output, fixed point, source drift and duplicate refusal. The two changed existing metadata inputs and existing Java owner also exercised missing-input refusal. Both current-base original and final wrapper sources passed the same frozen 123500/288223/3757 family and independent checks, with identical public javap output. Four known navigation/range counterexamples still fail identically and are explicitly negative evidence.

The current source image proof passes: 91 original module sources, seven optional primitive sources, two actual JMODs, original JNI ABI, and host plus linked-image Java/native oracles. The original packager remains unchanged. This is a distinct current-base qualification; the earlier 970a343 image records below are retained with their original pin.

The complete existing current-base Maven module ran 180 tests with three failures, zero errors and zero skips. All three failures belong to the concurrently added M3LongTreeSetTest. The exact same three failures were reproduced on untouched current-base source (seven tests, three failures). Full original-module Maven qualification therefore remains blocked. Its failed lifecycle also prevents installing that original dependency for the new optional Maven test lane; that lane is not claimed as a fresh-base Maven pass. The independent current Java/JNI/JMOD/image and changed-wrapper checks above passed. No tests or original gates were weakened.

Current receipts and exact logs are under `current-owner-reconciliation/`. Earlier prospective optional generic recipe resources remain reproducible historical evidence for their original no-owner pin. They are not the current product delivery recipe. The portable Synexia two-file refinements remain unchanged and fully qualified.

# Qualified filtered and sorted collection delivery

The portable changes refine two existing Synexia owners. M3FilteredViews removes
only private temporary view/entry construction while preserving the exact backing
iterator path, predicate order, exceptions and read-only mutation contract.
PrimitiveIndexView retains a call-local selected array when its length already
matches the selected count, preserving callback/version/defensive-copy behavior.

The frozen family oracles execute against the original, both serial refinements
and the composed final postimage. The final recipes use one combined crate per
changed source, so every step accepts the final postimage unchanged. Their named
entry points are `com.synexia.m3.M3FilteredWrapperPrivateConstruction20261017` and
`com.synexia.m3.M3PrimitiveIndexFilterExactFit20261017`.

The receiving `com.synexia.m3.M3JdkCollectionPack20261017` recipe projects the
qualified mechanics into the optional `jdk.m3.collections` module and existing
`com.m3.util` owners. Reuse the separately qualified text crate
`m3-optional-collections-registration-qualified-20261017` for the two optional
profile/name-mapping registrations. Existing java.util APIs and existing JNI
owners are unchanged. The original source and code/licensing boundaries remain
authoritative; no alternate collection engine or native ABI is introduced.

## Executed evidence

The original read-only oracle executes 123500 checks, mutable oracle 288223,
independent wrapper oracle 3757, and primitive oracle 798846 across eight kinds.
Synexia's original JNI owner also passes the frozen long selection/mutable
oracles. The M3 target runs its original M3IndexMaskCompactorSelfTest with 16925
checks and JNI=true on the host and linked image under -Xcheck:jni. The target
Maven test lane uses the original source-built JUnit coordinates and runs three
tests with zero failures/errors/skips.

An isolated receiver rebuilt 89 exact Git-blob-verified original inputs plus
the 21 collection/profile files, using the original baseline jmod_pack.py.
That independent offline Maven/image run passed. Thus this collection delivery
does not depend on the separately developed compiler, build-plan or packer work.
It compiles both actual collection modules, builds their JMODs, validates the
linked image and repeats its Java/native oracles there. Original sources and
exact original native exports remain in charge.

The measured primitive full-selection fixture saves 4112 bytes/op for 1024 rows
on the qualified JDK21 run. Half-selection allocation is unchanged. No default
JVM allocation saving was observed for the generic wrapper fixtures; a diagnostic
run with escape analysis disabled confirms only the eliminated construction.
No latency or throughput improvement is claimed.

Four frozen nullable-navigation/range counterexamples are retained as expected
negative evidence, not counted as passing correctness cases. Full custom JDK,
HotSpot, jtreg, CDS, cross-platform/native and whole-family 99-percent promotion
remain separate from this optional module qualification.

## Reproduction and custody

Use the bounded Maven SDK proof in `synexia-openrewrite-recipes/verification/m3-build-shared-ast-20261017`. It executes the four existing
canonical source owners identified by CANONICAL_ENGINE_CUSTODY.json. The two
original changed sources are retained under baseline-source-custody as `.txt`
evidence for exact private-source-independent recipe replay. Their final
postimages are already in the canonical resource templates. Source and licence
notices are preserved, including the genuine JUnit/APIGuardian parser contexts.

The public receiving snapshot belongs under the existing vendor owner at
`m3/vendor/synexia/snapshots/m3-build-collections-20261017`. It receives exact
canonical engines, resources and proof bytes; it does not overwrite the older
seed snapshot. Its catalogue and runtime promotion obligations are separate.
CANONICAL_SDK_EVIDENCE.json embeds exact receipt/log/Surefire text with individual
SHA-256 values and phase labels. Earlier frozen evidence is retained verbatim;
the provenance ledger identifies generated postimages, donor/parser sources,
frozen proof history and newly authored metadata separately.
